description: Reconstructs Uruk’s growth through irrigation, specialized labor, monumental precincts and regional exchange. Traces accounting from tokens and seals to proto-cuneiform tablets and scribal lists, then distinguishes the archaeological city from later Gilgamesh traditions and examines how excavation and preservation shape the surviving record.

period.note: Main fourth-millennium urban development and the narrated approximately 3350–3000 BCE proto-cuneiform archive. Earlier Ubaid communities, later legendary Gilgamesh traditions and modern excavations are separate context, not dates for the founding of Uruk.
